datapath.summary: The measured bottleneck is the blocking load path: a one-outstanding load service, a response bubble on hits, full-line-before-response refill, and an 8KiB direct-mapped cache.

storage_elements.name: load_queue
storage_elements.description: Load metadata and frozen store forwarding

storage_elements.name: dcache
storage_elements.description: Baseline 8KiB direct-mapped cache; parameter sweep up to 2048 lines

datapath.buffering_behavior: Keep one external read owner but pipeline cache hits and return the critical refill word before the remaining line words complete.
datapath.data_flow: LoadQueue -> DCache lookup -> hit/critical refill response -> completion bypass -> scoreboard -> commit

control.summary: Replace the response-only state with a pulse, allow response plus next load start, and add refill word count/early-response state.

fsm_list.name: dcache_fsm
fsm_list.key_transitions: Hit remains IDLE with registered response; miss refills critical word first and responds once before final line validation.

control.scheduling: Committed stores retain priority; a load response may release the active slot while the next queued load starts in the same cycle.
control.update_ordering: Old response completion precedes new active metadata installation; line valid is written only after refill_count reaches three.

performance_constraints.throughput: Target srcWithMext IPC >= 0.8; pipelined hit throughput one load per cycle after fill.
performance_constraints.latency: Return critical miss word on its first DRAM response; avoid a dedicated hit response bubble.
performance_constraints.folding_factor: Single issue and single commit remain fixed.

low_power.clock_gating: No new clock gating in this iteration; prefer BRAM inference over resettable flop arrays.

power_domains.name: cpu_clk
power_domains.description: Core and data memory clock domain

low_power.retention_requirements: Cache data is not reset; valid bits define usability.

hazards_and_ordering.description: Response and next request may share a cycle.
hazards_and_ordering.resolution: Complete old transaction before replacing active metadata.

hazards_and_ordering.description: Background refill still owns the ID-less external read channel.
hazards_and_ordering.resolution: Block new memory requests until all four words drain.

hazards_and_ordering.description: Flush may occur before or after early response.
hazards_and_ordering.resolution: Kill/drain prevents post-flush fill and duplicate completion.

verification_sensitive.behavior: Critical word response is emitted exactly once.
verification_sensitive.why_sensitive: Duplicate completion can corrupt a reused transaction ID.
verification_sensitive.suggested_coverage: Miss each of four word offsets plus flush before/after first response.

verification_sensitive.behavior: Response and new hit request overlap.
verification_sensitive.why_sensitive: Incorrect NBA priority can clear the newly installed active load.

verification_sensitive.behavior: Line valid only after all refill words.
verification_sensitive.why_sensitive: Premature hit exposes stale array contents.
verification_sensitive.suggested_coverage: Access another word in the line during and immediately after refill.

architecture_risks.risk: Large asynchronous data arrays may fail 200MHz or infer excessive LUTRAM.
architecture_risks.mitigation: Use synchronous byte-write banks and verify routed inference.

architecture_risks.risk: A larger scoreboard can improve memory overlap but lengthen the RAW critical path.
architecture_risks.mitigation: Keep depth 8 until routed timing and stall data justify change.
